values.products-description:
A hardcover A5 notebook bound in charcoal book linen, with 192 pages of 90 gsm ivory paper printed with a faint 5 mm dot grid. The paper takes fountain pen ink without feathering and shows only a ghost of it on the reverse.

The spine is sewn in signatures, so the book opens flat from the first page to the last. A black elastic band keeps it shut in a bag, and a rear pocket holds loose receipts and the odd pressed leaf.

We number every page and leave two blank for an index, because the notes you need most are the ones you wrote three months ago.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Charcoal linen A5 notebook with a black elastic band

products-image2.products-image2-alt: The notebook open to blank dotted pages

products-spec.products-spec-care: Keep dry; wipe the cover with a dry cloth
products-spec.products-spec-material: Book linen over board; 90 gsm ivory paper

values.products-subtitle: Linen-bound, dotted, and flat on the first page.

values.products-description:
A 30 cm straightedge milled from a single bar of solid brass, with millimetre and centimetre marks cut into the face rather than printed on it. The marks will outlast the desk.

At nearly 200 g the rule stays put when you draw against it and holds a book open at the page you are copying from. The edges are broken by hand so it is kind to fingers and paper.

Left alone, the brass darkens to a soft brown within a season. Rub it with a cloth and a little polish if you prefer it bright.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Solid brass 30 cm ruler with engraved marks

products-spec.products-spec-care: Let it patina, or polish with a soft cloth

values.products-subtitle: Solid brass, engraved millimetres, heavy enough to hold a page.

values.products-description:
A short fountain pen turned from aircraft aluminium and finished in a matte black anodise that will not show fingerprints. Capped, it fits a shirt pocket; posted, it balances like a full-size pen.

The steel nib is a medium-fine that writes wet enough for good paper and dry enough for cheap paper. It takes standard international cartridges or the included converter, so you are never far from ink.

The cap threads on in one and a half turns and seals well enough to leave in a bag for a month without drying out.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Matte black aluminium fountain pen, capped

products-image2.products-image2-alt: The pen uncapped, showing its steel nib

products-spec.products-spec-care: Flush with cool water between ink colours
products-spec.products-spec-dimensions: 118 mm capped, 145 mm posted, 12 mm diameter
products-spec.products-spec-warranty: Two years; nibs replaced free for the first year

values.products-subtitle: A machined aluminium fountain pen that posts, clips and travels.

values.products-description:
Cut from a single piece of dark Welsh slate and honed to a soft matte face, this tray gives paper clips, keys and a watch somewhere to live that is not the middle of your desk.

The floor is sunk 8 mm, just enough to stop things rolling off, and the underside carries four cork feet so the stone never scratches wood.

No two trays are quite the same colour. Some carry a faint grey seam through the stone, which we consider a feature.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Shallow dark slate desk tray holding two paper clips

products-spec.products-spec-care: Wipe with a damp cloth; a drop of oil deepens the colour

values.products-subtitle: A shallow tray of honed slate for the small things on a desk.

values.products-description:
A small cross-body pouch in black waxed cotton canvas that sheds rain and softens with use. It carries a phone, a wallet, keys and a notebook, and refuses anything more, which is the point.

The strap adjusts through a matte steel buckle and sits flat against the body. Inside, one slip pocket keeps cards apart from keys.

The wax wears in where you touch it. Re-wax once a year and the canvas will keep its shape for a decade.

products-spec.products-spec-care: Brush off dirt; re-wax once a year
products-spec.products-spec-material: Waxed cotton canvas; leather trim; steel buckle
products-spec.products-spec-warranty: Five years on seams and hardware

values.products-subtitle: Waxed canvas, one buckle, and room for exactly what you need.

values.products-description:
A slim card wallet cut from black full-grain leather and stitched with waxed linen thread. It holds up to six cards and a folded note, and it still slips into a front pocket without a bulge.

The leather is vegetable tanned, so it darkens and takes a polish with use rather than cracking. Edges are burnished by hand.

We make it in one size because we tried three and everyone chose this one.

products-spec.products-spec-care: Condition twice a year with a neutral balm
products-spec.products-spec-material: Vegetable-tanned full-grain leather; waxed linen thread

values.products-subtitle: Two pockets, one fold of leather, six cards at most.

values.products-description:
A short loop of black bridle leather riveted around a blackened steel split ring. It hangs from a belt loop or a bag strap and keeps your keys from scratching everything else in the pocket.

The ring opens with a thumbnail and holds up to eight keys. The rivet is solid copper, peened by hand, and will not work loose.

A small thing, but the one you touch most days.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Black leather key loop with a dark steel ring

products-spec.products-spec-care: Condition the leather when it looks dry
products-spec.products-spec-material: Bridle leather; blackened steel; copper rivet

values.products-subtitle: A leather loop and a blackened ring that keep keys quiet.

values.products-description:
A lightweight cape in charcoal ripstop nylon with a 10,000 mm waterproof coating and taped seams. It is cut long and wide enough to cover you and a bag on your back, and it vents at the sides so you do not boil in it.

Packed, it rolls into a stuff sack the size of a coffee cup. A hood with a stiffened brim keeps rain off glasses.

The first run sold through in a week. The next arrives in the autumn.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Folded charcoal rain cape beside its stuff sack

products-spec.products-spec-care: Rinse and hang to dry; do not tumble
products-spec.products-spec-material: Recycled ripstop nylon, PU coated; taped seams
products-spec.products-spec-warranty: Two years on seams and coating

values.products-subtitle: A charcoal cape that folds into its own sack and covers a bag.

values.products-description:
A small table lamp spun from brass with a hand-blown glass chimney. It burns lamp oil through a flat cotton wick and gives about the light of two candles, steady and warm, for eight hours on one filling.

A thumbwheel raises and lowers the wick, so you can turn it down to a glow at the end of the evening. The wide base will not tip on a desk.

It is the lamp in the photograph at the top of this shop, and the one we work by after dark.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Small lit brass oil lamp with a glass chimney

products-image2.products-image2-alt: The brass lamp unlit with its chimney set beside it

products-spec.products-spec-care: Trim the wick flat; burn only clear lamp oil
products-spec.products-spec-dimensions: 110 mm base, 240 mm tall with chimney
products-spec.products-spec-material: Spun brass; borosilicate glass chimney; cotton wick
products-spec.products-spec-warranty: Three years; chimneys replaced at cost

values.products-subtitle: A small brass oil lamp with a glass chimney and a steady flame.

values.products-description:
A pocket torch turned from black anodised aluminium, no longer than a key. One click gives a soft 30 lumen light for reading a map; a second gives 300 lumens for finding the path.

It charges over USB-C in an hour and runs for a week of evening walks on one charge. The lens is frosted, so the beam is even rather than a hot spot.

The tail stands flat, so it can point at the ceiling and light a small room.

products-spec.products-spec-care: Keep the port dry; charge every few months in storage

values.products-subtitle: A short aluminium torch with one button and two brightnesses.

values.products-description:
Three pillar candles poured from a blend of rapeseed and beeswax, in 7, 10 and 13 cm heights. They are unscented, so they sit quietly beside dinner and do not argue with coffee.

The wax burns clean and slowly, about 40 hours for the tallest. Cotton wicks are pre-trimmed and stay centred to the end.

They arrive wrapped in paper, not plastic, in a box you can keep them in between evenings.

products-image1.products-image1-alt: Three ivory pillar candles of different heights

products-spec.products-spec-care: Trim wicks to 5 mm; never leave burning unattended
products-spec.products-spec-material: Rapeseed and beeswax blend; cotton wicks

values.products-subtitle: Three unscented ivory pillars in three heights.

values.products-description:
A reading light that clips to a book cover, a shelf or the edge of a bunk and bends its neck to where the page is. The warm 2700 K light is dimmable in three steps and never glares off paper.

The clip is lined with soft silicone so it will not mark a cover. It charges over USB-C and lasts twenty evenings of an hour each.

This batch is gone. We are waiting on new clips that grip thicker shelves.

products-spec.products-spec-care: Wipe clean; avoid bending the neck past 90°
products-spec.products-spec-material: ABS body; silicone-lined clip; steel gooseneck

values.products-subtitle: A small clip-on light with a flexible neck for books and bunks.

values.faq-answer: No. Nightjar Supply is a demo site built with [zudo-composer](https://github.com/Takazudo/zudo-composer). Nothing is for sale, nothing ships and no payment is ever taken.
The checkout form checks what you type, waits a moment and shows a made-up order number. Your cart is then emptied. **No data leaves your browser.**
values.faq-question: What happens when I check out?

values.faq-answer: In your browser's local storage, under one key. Clear your site data and the cart is gone. There is no account and no server-side basket.
In this demo, a flat 8 USD on every order, shown in the cart summary. A real shop would quote by weight and destination.
There is nothing to return. If this were a real shop, we would offer thirty days on anything unused, with a prepaid label.
Two products are marked sold out so the demo can show how the shop behaves when stock runs out: the badge changes and the add-to-cart button is disabled.
values.faq-question: Why do some products say sold out?

values.faq-answer: They are stylised illustrations made for this demo. Every product, maker and place name here is invented.
Every page is a Composer composition. Products, categories and these questions are Content entries, bound to components through Mappings and placed in a Sitemapper tree.

values.about-body:
## Twelve objects, no more

Nightjar Supply started with a lamp, a notebook and a pen on a workbench late at night. We wanted a shop that sold only the things that earn their place on that bench: tools for writing, carrying and seeing by.

Every object here is made by a small workshop we have visited. We keep the range to twelve so we can know each one well, and we would rather sell out than fill the shelf with things we do not use ourselves.

## How we choose

- It must do one job well and be quiet about it.
- It must get better with use, or at least not worse.
- It must be repairable, refillable or built to outlast its warranty.

## A demo, honestly

This shop is a demonstration of *zudo-composer*. The products, workshops and prices are invented, and the checkout sends nothing anywhere. The contact form below behaves the same way.
